**UI/UX Audit: AgentCanvas (Dark Mode, 1600x900)**

### 1. Visual Clutter & Dark Theme Overwhelm
The primary issue is **"Border Fatigue"** caused by the dark theme. In light mode, subtle borders often disappear into the background. Here, every UI element is defined by a high-contrast 1px border, creating a "grid of boxes" effect that fragments the visual field.
*   **The Dotted Box:** The central "Empty canvas" container uses a heavy dashed border. Against a dark background, this creates significant visual vibration (Moiré-like effect) and draws the eye away from the actual content area.
*   **Chip Saturation:** The right panel contains six distinct outlined chips ("Designs", "User Flows", etc.). In dark mode, these look like clickable buttons rather than passive tags, increasing cognitive load.
*   **Header Density:** The top bar contains three distinct functional zones (Global Nav, Project Context, View Controls) with almost no whitespace between them.

### 2. Floating Bottom Toolbar & Zoom Analysis
The bottom toolbar is **over-engineered for a default empty state**.
*   **Button Count:** There are 13 distinct icon buttons in the main toolbar group plus zoom controls. For a user staring at an empty canvas, seeing a full professional CAD/CAM toolset (Pen, Shapes, Text, Undo/Redo) is intimidating.
*   **Visual Weight:** The floating pill shape has a solid background and drop shadow that feels "heavy" compared to the minimalist aesthetic of modern canvas tools (like Figma or Linear).
*   **Redundancy:** The "Ask" button exists in both the top header and conceptually in the chat input. The "Pen" tool is selected in the top right but also available in the bottom bar.

### 3. Right Chat Panel Empty State
The panel fails the **"Progressive Disclosure"** test.
*   **Information Dump:** The "How does this work?" section is a wall of text (approx. 100 words) using small font on a dark background. It explains technical details about SDKs and API calls that a new user doesn't need to read immediately.
*   **Action Paralysis:** Presenting 6 preset categories *and* a text input *and* a "Try a preset prompt" button creates choice paralysis. The user doesn't know if they should read, click a chip, or type.
*   **Status Noise:** Showing "offline" status and model version (`kimi-k2-5`) in red/green dots adds anxiety to an onboarding screen.

### 4. Duplicated & Redundant UI
*   **Dual Entry Points:** The central canvas says "Describe what you want... or pick a shape from the toolbar." The right panel says "Ask the agent...". This splits the user's mental model between "Drawing" vs. "Prompting" without clarifying they are the same workflow.
*   **Navigation Duplication:** "Chats" is a top-level tab in the left sidebar, but also the active view. The "New chat" button is visually competing with the single existing chat item.
*   **Tool Indicators:** The "pen" tool is highlighted in the top-right metadata bar *and* implicitly selected in the bottom toolbar (if it were visible), creating redundant state indicators.

---

### Top 5 Concrete Simplifications

**1. Implement "Ghost" Toolbars (Contextual Appearance)**
Hide the bottom drawing toolbar completely when the canvas is empty. Show only the **Zoom controls** (- 100% + Reset). The drawing tools should only appear once the user has initiated a generation or manually switched to "Draw Mode." This reduces the initial UI footprint by ~40%.

**2. Collapse the Onboarding Card (Right Panel)**
Replace the text-heavy "How does this work?" block with a **single-line greeting**: *"Hi! I’m your design agent. What are we building today?"*
Move the 6 category chips into a **secondary "Browse prompts" dropdown** or hide them until the user clicks a "/" command in the input field. Remove the "Try a preset prompt" button entirely—merge this action into the input placeholder text: *"Type '/' for presets..."*

**3. Soften the Canvas Container**
Change the central "Empty canvas" box from a **dashed border** to a very subtle, solid 1px border in a color only slightly lighter than the background (`#2a2a2a` instead of `#444`). Alternatively, remove the border entirely and use a centered, low-opacity icon (opacity 0.3) to indicate the drop zone without creating a "boxy" feel.

**4. Unify the Input Mechanism**
Remove the "Try a preset prompt" button from the center of the canvas. Force all interaction through the **Right Panel Chat Input** to establish a single "Command Center." If you want to keep the center-prompt, make the right panel collapse or dim when the center button is hovered, indicating they are the same function.

**5. Declutter the Top Metadata Bar**
Remove the redundant **"Canvas · demo"** and **"completed"** badges from the top center. Move the **Fork** button into the "File" menu or a settings dropdown. The top bar should only show: `[Project Name] [Status Dot] [Search] [Ask Button] [User Avatar]`. This frees up 120px of horizontal space and removes 3 unnecessary UI elements.
